fields.name: QueryStatement.Create factory family
fields.contract: QueryStatement.Create returns Lazy<QueryStatement> so command text is not read until Value is requested. Every overload accepts a statement name; callers may omit parameter names, supply parameter names, select a folder and extension, or supply a full file path. When materialized, the result is a QueryStatement query contract whose name and parameter names are the supplied values and whose command type is Text. For the three overloads that do not take a full file path, the file location is computed at the moment Value is first evaluated (not when Create is called) from the statement name, a folder, and an extension: when the name itself is a rooted path, the folder is ignored and the path is taken from the name directly; otherwise, when the folder is a rooted path, the folder and name are combined directly; otherwise, the folder and name are combined relative to the application's base directory; in every case the extension is appended to the resulting file name whenever a non-null extension was supplied. The Create(name) and Create(name, parameterNames) overloads source the folder and extension from QueryStatement.Folder (default "SQL") and QueryStatement.Extension (default "sql") — static properties shared by the whole process, read at Value-evaluation time rather than at Create-call time, so a later reassignment can still change which file a previously-created Lazy<QueryStatement> loads. The four-argument overload instead takes an explicit folder and extension, bypassing those static defaults.
